Subject: Feature parity & competitive eval — next steps (streaming / tool-calls / structured outputs)

Thanks for the call today — great to meet the Acme team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same plan.

TL;DR: Redwood will run a focused feature parity + competitive evaluation in Acme staging comparing (a) tool/function calling behavior, (b) structured/JSON outputs (schema conformance), and (c) streaming response behavior and latency. We'll produce an evaluation matrix and a short write-up of differentiators vs the hyperscalers you mentioned.

What we agreed on:
- Acme will share a small sample dataset and 6 representative prompts (function call examples + structured output cases).
- Redwood will run three test tracks in Acme staging: function-calling correctness, structured-output schema validation, and streaming latency/behavior.
- We'll compare results to Hyperscaler A and Hyperscaler B using the same prompts (A/B runs).
- Target timeline: initial test results within 10 business days; tech sync after results to decide follow-ups.

Action items / owners:
- Sam / Jenna: share sample prompts + any DoD (data handling notes) by end of week.
- Chloe (engineering): set up test harness and run initial runs on Redwood staging (need sampling keys from Acme).
- Rishi (pricing): scope a short dedicated trial if we need throughput > hosted limits.
- Me (Marissa): coordinate logistics, collate results, and create comparatives vs other vendors.

Attached: acme-eval-matrix.xlsx (initial template), redwood-feature-notes.pdf (what to expect in each track).

Looking forward — propose a 30-min tech sync next Wed (Apr 6) to review initial results. If that works for you I’ll send an invite.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful and aligns with our ask. A couple clarifications: 

1) For function/tool calling we care about deterministic argument serialization (we have strict schema validation on our side). Will Redwood validate callable args and return standardized JSON so we can automatically route?
2) For streaming: our main KPI is median first-byte latency and end-to-end token throughput under a 1k token window. Can you capture these exact metrics?

We’ll share the sample prompts and a short dataset by Friday. Also attaching our internal schema examples so you can plan the structured-output tests.

Great — thanks Sam. Quick answers and proposed concrete test plan: 

- Deterministic args: yes — for function calling track we'll validate argument serialization and field-level types. We’ll run a golden set of 200 calls and report success/failure rates and example discrepancies.
- Streaming metrics: we will capture 50/95/99 latency percentiles for first byte and tail, plus token throughput at target window sizes (including your 1k token window).

Proposed initial test plan (what Redwood will run):
1) Function calling correctness: 200 calls across 10 function schemas (golden set). Report discrepancies and examples where model behavior differs from expected schema.
2) Structured output validation: run 150 prompts that require strict JSON output; measure schema conformance (schema-validator pass rate) and provide quick fixes (prompt templates).
3) Streaming/tool-calls latency: stream a subset of 50 long outputs and measure first-byte, median token latency under 1k window; we’ll also record quality deltas vs non-streamed runs.
4) Competitive A/B: run parallel tests against Hyperscaler A and Hyperscaler B using the same prompts and compute deltas on pass rates and latency.

Tech sync: Wed Apr 6 10:00am PT — I’ll send a calendar invite after you confirm.

Internal notes: Chloe — please use the attached eval matrix and start provisioning the staging runs once we receive sample prompts. Rishi — can you draft a short dedicated-trial estimate in case Acme needs higher throughput?

Thanks — Marissa

Looping in a few technical notes from the test-harness side: 

- For streaming tests we’ll enable chunked responses with token-level timestamps; that lets us compute per-token latencies and first-byte. We’ll also test with and without our KV prefix cache to see effects on latency.
- Function calling: we’ll run with strict type checking and an additional prompt-mangling step to detect brittle prompt shapes.
- Structured outputs: will use the JSON schema validator (latest draft) and produce both pass/fail counts and a set of minimal prompt patches to improve conformance.
- Competitive runs: to make apples-to-apples comparisons we’ll fix temperature/seed and use identical request shapes; differences in tokenization are noted in the matrix.

Request for Acme: please provide one canonical post-call sample per category (function call example, structured JSON example, and a long streaming example) and a short list of latency SLOs you care about.

I’ll begin wiring the harness this afternoon; will post a short design doc to the shared Drive link once ready.

—Chloe
